title: Caffeine runbook — mini log
content:
11/05 Morning notes (quick, messy)

Context: took over on infra triage after standup. New p99 spikes on small models in eu-west-1 (seen since 11/04 evening). Hypothesis: intermittent KV-cache churn + nvlink saturation during concurrent long-seq jobs.

Immediate observations:
- Alerts: tail-latency alert fired twice between 02:14-02:23 UTC on node gpu-9b. CPU metrics looked normal, but nvlink TX dropped ~30% for ~2m in the window.
- Request patterns: saw an increase in long-context translation jobs with sequence length ~8192 tokens (customer: locale-translations-prod). They came in bursts (4–6 concurrent).
- KV cache: eviction rate higher than expected for same model-version. Cache hits down from ~0.94 -> 0.78 in affected node.

Quick checklist (what I did):
- Replayed a request sample locally (mini trace) and confirmed longer memcpys at keypoints -> suggests cross-GPU shuffles (nvlink).
- Rolled the serving route for the model to a variant with aggressive prefix caching (v1.3 -> v1.3-prefetch) for a subset of traffic (canary 10%).
- Captured perf profile (flamegraph) and attached to PR 482.

Open hypotheses to validate (ranked):
1) NVLink contention when multiple long-seq jobs coincide on same host (most likely based on nvlink tx dips).
2) KV-cache throttling interaction with batching: when cache miss rate spikes, batching engine increases batch size which amplifies nvlink pressure.
3) Root cause could be an upstream router that does uneven spreading causing hotspot on gpu-9b.

Immediate TODOs (short term)
- [ ] Run isolated replay on gpu-9b with identical workload but pinned to one process to measure nvlink baseline (no other pods). (noah volunteered to run this).
- [ ] Add a short-lived metric: per-model nvlink-utilization (sample every 10s) to understand correlation. (Ivy to set up).
- [ ] Increase canary to 25% for v1.3-prefetch if latency stays within SLO for next 30m. (me)
- [ ] Add log markers in runtime to tag KV-cache eviction events with request IDs. Helps tie to user traces. (follow-up PR)

Commands / snippets I ran (notes):
- capture traces: ./tools/capture_invocation --node gpu-9b --sample 50 --out /tmp/gpu9b-scans
- nvlink counters: nvidia-smi nvlink --query --format=csv
- quick replay (local): PYTHONPATH=. python tools/replay_sample.py --sample /tmp/gpu9b-scans/sample_07.json --pin-gpu 9

Small triage timeline: 
- 02:05 alert -> paged oncall -> quick look: nvlink dips -> started canary on prefetched variant at 02:28 -> 02:40 latency normalized on canary traffic.

Notes for kernel TODO (tech):
- Investigate whether the kernel uses per-stream host pinned buffers for KV-cache copies. If copies are host and then nvlink they double-transfer; maybe try remapping to cudaMemcpyPeer where possible.
- Explore batching scheduler: add a cap that prevents batch growth above N when measured nvlink util > X%. (Risk: throughput reduction, but acceptable fallback for tail-latency).
- Check NUMA/cpu-affinity for the process on gpu-9b. Found process pinned to socket 0 but memory allocs on interleaved nodes -> could hurt DMA throughput.

Unresolved questions (for sync with infra):
- Is there any maintenance or noisy neighbor (backups, K8s daemon job) on gpu-9b during that window? (infra)
- Did model runner upgrade happen 11/03 -> any runtime flags changed? (release eng)

Next steps (today):
- 09:30 sync with Noah & Ivy (standup follow up) to assign replay jobs and metric setup.
- 11:00 run through PR 482 changes and add KV eviction log tags (small PR).
- Afternoon: if canary still fine, promote to 25% and watch for 1h. If regressions, route fallback to model v1.2-stable.

Personal notes to self:
- Keep the runbook short; convert to confluence page if we need runbook steps persistently.
- When adding nvlink metrics, avoid high-cardinality labels; keep it aggregated per-host and per-model.

Random scratch ideas (brain dump):
- Could precompute low-cost embeddings for common prefixes and serve them from host memory to avoid repeated KV-cache miss storms.
- A lightweight admission controller that refuses additional long-seq requests when host nvlink > threshold; queue them in a backlog with estimated start.
summary: Morning triage for intermittent p99 spikes; hypotheses: nvlink contention + kv-cache churn; immediate canary to prefetched variant, plan to add nvlink metrics + eviction tags; follow-ups assigned to Noah and Ivy.
